headlines.title: Visa Expands AI-Powered Payments Programme to More Than 140 Merchants and Payment Providers
headlines.summary: Visa (NYSE:V) has expanded its Agentic Ready programme to include merchants, payment processors, acquiring banks and commerce platforms, extending its efforts to support transactions initiated by artificial intelligence agents.

headlines.title: PayPal Holdings (PYPL) Expands AI Driven Token Payments Acceptance
headlines.summary: PayPal Holdings (NasdaqGS: PYPL) has partnered with Visa to expand support for AI-driven agentic token payments. The collaboration aims to let AI agents initiate tokenized Visa payments through PayPal's wallet and merchant acceptance network. The move aligns PayPal with sector wide efforts to build secure, programmable payment rails for autonomous digital transactions. This new PayPal and Visa push into AI driven token payments is worth weighing alongside the rest of our findings.

headlines.title: Lianlian DigiTech and Visa Advance Trusted B2B Agentic Commerce for Small and Medium-Sized Businesses
headlines.summary: Lianlian DigiTech (HKEX: 2598) and Visa (NYSE: V), a global leader in digital payments, today announced the next phase of their collaboration to advance trusted B2B agentic commerce. The companies have completed their first live transaction in Asia Pacific through Visa Intelligent Commerce Connect,[ii] using a tokenised payment credential designed specifically for an authorised AI agent.

headlines.title: Visa Expands Agentic Ready to Help Scale Trusted AI Commerce Globally
headlines.summary: SAN FRANCISCO, November 18, 2026--Visa (NYSE: V), a world leader in digital payments, today announced the expansion of the Visa Agentic Ready program to the acceptance ecosystem. As a part of Visa Intelligent Commerce, the expanded program helps merchants, payment service providers (PSPs), and acquirers prepare for agent-initiated transactions and participate in the next era of commerce.

headlines.title: Visa Launches Threat Intelligence Platform to Strengthen Cyber and Fraud Defense
headlines.summary: Fraud is widely recognized as a downstream outcome of earlier cyber incidents, often beginning with data compromise, credential theft, or system exploitation well before a transaction is initiated[1]. Organizations that manage cybersecurity and fraud as separate events may find it hard to act fast on threats before they lead to losses.

description: Visa Inc. operates as a payment technology company in the United States and internationally. The company operates VisaNet, a transaction processing network that enables authorization, clearing, and settlement of payment transactions. It also offers credit, debit, and prepaid card products; tap to pay, tokenization, and click to pay services; Visa Direct, a platform which facilitates money movement, enabling clients to collect, hold, convert, and send funds across its network; and issuing solutions, such as airport lounge access, dining reservations, shopping experiences, event tickets, and seller offers. In addition, the company provides acceptance solutions, an omnichannel payment integration with e-commerce platforms; risk detection and prevention solutions; and advisory and other services comprising consulting practice, proprietary analytics models, data scientists and economists, marketing services, and managed services. It provides its services under the Visa, Visa Electron, V PAY, Interlink, and PLUS brands. The company serves consumers, sellers, financial institutions, and government entities. Visa Inc. was founded in 1958 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California.
